name: augeas
why: Its lens-based model parses config files into trees and back, an unusual way of treating every config as structured data.

brief.what_it_is: Augeas is a configuration editing tool. It parses configuration files in their native formats and transforms them into a tree. Changes are made by manipulating that tree and saving it back into the native config files. The homepage describes it as a C library API, a shell command-line tool for scripts, language bindings for scripting languages, canonical tree representations of common config files, and a domain-specific language for describing config file formats. The Homebrew executables are augmatch, augparse, augprint, augtool, and fadot.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the goal is to manipulate configuration files more safely than the ad-hoc grep, sed, and awk techniques commonly used in scripts, and to provide a local configuration API for Linux. It also aims to make it easy to integrate new config files into the Augeas tree.
brief.how_it_works: Lenses, written in Augeas's domain-specific language, describe each config file format and map it to and from a canonical tree. Edits go to the tree, and Augeas writes the tree back out as native config text. The homepage does not go into further detail, and I did not fetch the Quick Tour or documentation pages.
brief.install_notes: Homebrew installs lenses to $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/augeas/lenses/dist, according to the brew caveat. No other setup, runtime, or account requirements were visible on the homepage.
brief.standout: Most config tools treat files as text to be patched with regular expressions. Augeas instead parses each file into a tree using a per-format lens and writes it back, so scripts edit structured data. The lens language is what makes new formats pluggable.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage has a Releases link and a Todo list link, but it shows no release date, version, or last-commit date, and I did not follow those links.
brief.caveats: The homepage describes the Linux focus as a goal, and it does not state platform support beyond that. I did not read the README, docs, or release notes, so I have no build or install details beyond the brew caveat. The homepage was reachable, so no fallback was needed.

entry.title: Augeas
entry.tldr: Augeas parses config files into a tree and writes them back, so scripts edit structured data instead of patching text with sed.
entry.deeper_look:
Augeas reads configuration files in their native formats and turns them into a tree. You change the tree, then save it, and Augeas writes the native config text back out. It ships as a C library, a shell tool for scripts (`augtool`), and bindings for scripting languages. The Homebrew formula also installs `augmatch`, `augparse`, `augprint` and `fadot`.

The homepage states the motivation plainly: manipulate config files "safer than the ad-hoc techniques generally used with grep, sed, awk and similar mechanisms in scripting languages". It also aims to provide a local configuration API for Linux.

The idea underneath is the lens. A lens is a small program in Augeas's own domain-specific language that describes one file format and maps it to and from a canonical tree. Because the same description drives both parsing and writing, the tool can save a file back out as native text. Supporting a new file means writing a new lens, which the project says it wants to make easy.

That makes it a door into bidirectional parsing: treating every config file, whatever its quirks, as the same kind of structured data.
entry.install:
brew install augeas
# Lenses are installed to $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/augeas/lenses/dist
